sn42.2:1.2: His verses at [thag19.1]() speak eloquently of the tension between the worldly and the spiritual life. | The name _tālapuṭa_ is explained by the commentary as due to his face being the color of a fresh palmyra fruit. This, however, leaves the element _puṭa_ (“pouch”) unexplained. _Tālapuṭa_ is known in Jain texts as a kind of poison (Uttarādhyayana Sūtra 16, verse 13; Isibhāsiyāiṁ 10.13; Triṣaṣṭiśalākāpuruṣa Caritra 1.2). _Tāla_ can mean “yellow orpiment”, a kind of arsenic used for coloring ([thig14.1:28.1]()), so _tālapuṭa_ could mean “pouch of arsenic”.
sn42.2:1.4: Re saccalika, I follow BB and the comm. even though “distortion of the truth” seems like a better meaning, sacca and alika always occur as a contrastive pair, supporting the comm.
